Use the existing topk_ids/topk_weights as inputs for generation 1, but structure the kernel around per-expert problem sizes so it can consume the scheduling metadata from child 1_0 in later iterations. strategy.expected_impact: Can remove the separate finalize launch, reduce split atomic traffic, and improve locality for gemm2_weights and scales by processing contiguous expert tiles. It also aligns the CUDA candidate with FlashInfer's grouped finalize boundary while keeping GEMM1 unchanged for attribution.
strategy.risks: A full tensor-core path may not be available on the L20D/Ada-like target for native FP4, so the first version may still use software FP4 dequant inside a tiled GEMM. T=1 gives tiny per-expert M, so occupancy and tail effects are serious. Keep correctness by preserving weighted scatter-add semantics when multiple top-k entries map to the same source token.
